Every golden or vector under `tests/goldens/` and `tests/vectors/` lists its generator, the tool versions it depends on, and a volatility grade (1 = deterministic everywhere; 5 = expected to drift). Regeneration is `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest <test> -k <name>` followed by a commit whose message names the tool version that moved it.

| `tests/goldens/toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden` | `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py -k golden` (the canonical transcript of `cairn.selftest.run_once`, hex, one line per corpus case and per arm) | PARI 2.17.4, cypari2 2.2.4, gp binary, blake3 1.0.9 | 3 | Six lines: four corpus cases then the postcondition and verifier arms. Byte-equal across the double run, since no timestamp enters the transcript and the seed, hashers and clock are pinned. The grade is 3 rather than 2 because the seeded arm draws from `H(implementation_revision || 'selftest-seed')`, so the arm's curve and therefore this file move whenever any path in `toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES` changes: `src/cairn/pari.py`, `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py`, `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json`. That coupling is the point. A revision that moves the transcript needs a fresh certificate, so the regeneration and the re-mint land in one attributed commit naming the source that moved. The bundle hash is deliberately absent, which keeps the file stable across bundle rebuilds. |
| `tests/goldens/toy_curve_floor.golden` | same command, `-k golden` | PARI 2.17.4, cypari2 2.2.4, gp binary | 2 | `{pass: 4, floor: 4, arms: {postcondition: pass, verifier: {ok: 20, fail: 20}}}`. Counts only, so it is independent of the implementation revision. Only an attributed change may raise the floor, which is PLAN section 2's rule; `pass_floor` itself lives in `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json`. |
| `tests/goldens/toy_curve_certificate.golden` | same command, `-k certificate_golden` | PARI 2.17.4, cypari2 2.2.4, gp binary, libpari, host OS | 4 | Holds the certificate together with the identity bundle hash, env manifest hash, transcript hash and implementation revision it was minted under. It folds in `env_manifest_hash`, which depends on libpari, the gp binary digest and the OS, so the recorded value is valid for the recorded platform only. The test recomputes the certificate from the golden transcript hash plus the live identity and env hashes and asserts the live certificate equals that recomputation; it asserts equality with the recorded certificate only when the live identity and env hashes both match the recorded pair. |
| `tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden` | `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py -k bundle_hash_golden` (`cairn.bundle.build` over `bundle/*.json` plus `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp` and `lean/lake-manifest.json`, twice under tmp_path) | none (BLAKE3 over canonical bytes; no PARI, no sqlite content in the hash) | 2 | Hashed sources: `bundle/allow_lists.json`, `bundle/auditor.json`, `bundle/gate_plan.json`, `bundle/ladder_plan.json`, `bundle/lean.json`, `bundle/role_templates.json`, `bundle/tiers.json`, `bundle/verifier.json`, `bundle/waivable_checks.json`, `bundle/scrutiny.json` (the `scrutiny` object: the proportional-scrutiny router's target family, generic-bound exponent, classes and top-class obligations), `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`, `lean/lake-manifest.json` (the `lake_manifest` object: the mathlib revision `bundle/lean.json` pins and every dependency revision it inherits, as `lake update` wrote them), `bundle/challenge_prelude.lean` and `src/cairn/challenge.py` (the `challenge_prelude` and `challenge_renderer` objects, raw bytes like the verifier script, so an edited prelude or renderer is a different bundle), `bundle/container.json` (the `container` object: the gold-tier image's pinned inputs) and `bundle/Containerfile` (the `container_file` raw object; the two together are the input-addressed container identity, PLAN §16 decision 14). Deterministic and platform-independent: the bundle holds strings, ints, bools, nulls and bytes only, `backend_path` among them as a string. It moves only when a bundle source changes, which is an operator act, so a regenerated golden lands only with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` in an attributed commit naming the source that moved. A `lake update` in `lean/` is such an act. The deploy-time copy of this rule is the pin. |
| `tests/goldens/m0_run_transcript.golden` | `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py -k transcript` (the ordered `cairn` log records of `cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` after the operator sequence, scrubbed by `scrub()` in `tests/conftest.py`) | PARI/GP 2.17.4, libpari 2.17.2, cypari2 2.2.4, blake3 1.0.9 | 2 | Shape-deterministic: one line per gate-plan step with its expected and observed verdict, one per M0 slice step, one per verifier arm with its reason codes, and one for the submitter-named refusal carrying `spawned=False`. Every 64-hex digest scrubs to `[HASH]`, every 32-hex id to `[ID]`, `wall_ms` to `[MS]`, tmp paths to `[PATH]`, and the bundle digest to `[BUNDLE]`, so it holds across machines and runs. It moves when a step is added or removed, when a verdict or reason vocabulary changes, or when the gate bundle's plan changes; it does not move with timings, hashes or paths. A regeneration lands only in an attributed commit naming which step or vocabulary moved. |

The `gate_bundle_hash.golden` source inventory also includes the raw objects
`lean/Cairn/StatementHash.lean` (`lean_statement_hasher`) and
`lean/Cairn/Axioms.lean` (`lean_axiom_checker`). Their source bytes are registered by
`cairn.bundle.source_objects`; the hasher and axiom provenance rows above carry the
pinned toolchain and their own expected-output vectors. Editing either source moves
the bundle golden and requires an attributed regeneration.
